answer: Each identity enters consensus only through a bonded admission inlet. It locks unreusable stake and posts a unique work packet whose hash binds its address and a fresh nonce. Established peers re-execute that packet and countersign only when the output and still-locked stake match; a copied packet is refused at any second inlet. Correlated packets from one operator collapse into a single dune of work and are slashed together. Standing requires a lotus quorum of attestors with mutually uncorrelated histories, so every extra identity pays new capital, new unique work, and slash risk.
